question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

Air Travel is the _______ growing emitter of climate change gases.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. fastest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank comes immediately after the definite article "the" and before the participle "growing". The structure "the + superlative + growing" is required here, so the superlative degree "fastest" is correct.

◦ Correct: Air Travel is the fastest growing emitter of climate change gases.

• "Fastest growing" is a fixed collocation meaning increasing more quickly than anything else. (सबसे तेज़ी से बढ़ने वाला)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "fasting" means abstaining from food — completely unrelated in meaning.

• Option 3 "fastly" is not a word in standard English; the adverb form of "fast" is simply "fast".

• Option 4 "fast" (positive degree) cannot follow "the" in this comparison-type structure — "the fast growing emitter" is ungrammatical.

NOTE

• Degrees of "fast": fast – faster – fastest. The superlative always takes "the": the fastest runner, the fastest growing economy.

• "Fast" is one of those words that is both an adjective and an adverb (he runs fast), so "fastly" never exists.

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

A diagram showing the path of planets
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Zodiac.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Zodiac" is a diagram/belt of the heavens showing the apparent paths of the sun, moon and planets, divided into twelve signs. (राशिचक्र)

◦ Example: The zodiac is divided into twelve signs, from Aries to Pisces.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Horoscope" is a forecast of a person's future based on the position of stars at his/her birth — a prediction, not a diagram of planetary paths. (जन्मकुंडली)

• Option 3 "Planetarium" is a building/dome in which images of stars and planets are projected for viewing. (तारामंडल भवन)

• Option 4 "Platitude" means a dull, overused remark or statement. (घिसा-पिटा कथन)

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: Astronomy (scientific study of heavenly bodies), Astrology (study of the influence of stars on human affairs), Observatory (a place for observing celestial bodies), Orbit (path of a body around another).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

We didn't mean to _____ all of you waiting.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. keep.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed expression is "keep somebody waiting", which means to make a person wait for you. (किसी को इंतज़ार कराना)

◦ Correct: We didn't mean to keep all of you waiting.

• The structure is keep + object + V-ing (keep them waiting / keep the engine running).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "make" is tempting but "make" is followed by the bare infinitive, not "-ing" — "make you wait", never "make you waiting". Since the sentence already has "waiting", "make" is wrong.

• Option 1 "creep" (to move slowly and quietly) and Option 3 "seep" (of liquid, to flow slowly through small openings) make no sense here.

NOTE

• Useful patterns: keep + object + V-ing (keep him waiting), make + object + bare infinitive (make him wait), let + object + bare infinitive (let him wait), get + object + to-infinitive (get him to wait).

question:
Select the appropriate antonym for the underlined word.

A war has been unleashed on financial untouchability.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. confined.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Unleashed" means released, set free, let loose (a force or feeling) suddenly and without restraint. (छोड़ देना / मुक्त कर देना)

• Its antonym is "confined", which means kept within limits; restricted; shut in. (सीमित / बंद किया हुआ)

◦ Example: The dog was unleashed in the park but later confined to its kennel.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "unchained" (freed from chains) is a synonym of unleashed, not an antonym.

• Option 4 "free" is likewise a synonym in sense.

• Option 3 "regarded" (considered/looked upon) is unrelated to the idea of release or restraint.

NOTE

• Synonyms of unleash: release, let loose, set free, unbridle, trigger.

• Antonyms of unleash: confine, restrain, curb, check, suppress, leash.

question: Choose the sentence with no spelling error.
option_1: Service industreis relie on a set of processes.
option_2: Service industries rely on a set of processes.
option_3: Servise industries rely on a set of processes.
option_4: Service industries rely on a set of procceses.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Service industries rely on a set of processes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Only Option 2 spells every word correctly — "Service", "industries", "rely" and "processes".

◦ Correct: Service industries rely on a set of processes.

• Spelling keys: SER + VICE; IN + DUS + TRIES (industry → industries); RE + LY; PRO + CES + SES.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 has two errors: "industreis" → industries, and "relie" → rely.

• Option 3 misspells "Servise" → Service.

• Option 4 misspells "procceses" → processes.

NOTE

• Nouns ending in a consonant + "-y" change the "y" to "-ies" in the plural: industry → industries, city → cities, company → companies.

• "Process" ends in "-ss", so the plural adds "-es": process → processes.

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

Out of the woods
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Out of danger.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "out of the woods" means out of danger or difficulty; past the critical or risky stage. (संकट से बाहर होना)

◦ Example: The patient's fever has come down, but the doctors say he is not yet out of the woods.

• It is most often used in the negative — "not out of the woods yet" — to say that the danger has not fully passed.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "To lose contact" corresponds to idioms such as "lose touch with".

• Option 3 "To meet with disaster" is close to "come a cropper" or "go to the dogs".

• Option 4 "Not adhering to rules" is close to "play fast and loose" or "cut corners".

NOTE

• Related idioms of danger/safety: "out of the frying pan into the fire" (from one trouble into a worse one), "on thin ice" (in a risky position), "a close shave" (a narrow escape), "high and dry" (stranded).

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Just because I am quiet doesn't mean I can't scold you.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. No error.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "Just because I am quiet doesn't mean I can't scold you." is grammatically correct in every part, so "No error" is the right choice.

◦ "Just because ..." functions as the subject clause and takes the singular verb "doesn't mean" — this is correct.

◦ "quiet" (silent, not talkative) is the right word and the right spelling; the verb after "can't" is correctly the bare infinitive "scold".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Segment 1 "Just because I am" — correct; "because" properly introduces the reason clause.

• Segment 4 "quiet doesn't mean" — correct; note that "quiet" (शांत) must not be confused with "quite" (काफ़ी) or "quit" (छोड़ना).

• Segment 3 "I can't scold you." — correct; "can't" is followed by the base form "scold".

NOTE

• The pattern "Just because X, (it) doesn't mean Y" is a standard English construction used to deny a wrong inference — e.g., "Just because he is rich doesn't mean he is happy."

• In error-spotting questions, always check: subject–verb agreement, tense, preposition, article, spelling and word choice — if all are sound, "No error" is the answer.

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

The home I ______ with my husband in 1986 still smelled like him.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. had shared.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The main clause is in the simple past ("still smelled like him"). The act of sharing the home in 1986 happened before that past moment, so the earlier action takes the past perfect — "had shared".

◦ Correct: The home I had shared with my husband in 1986 still smelled like him.

• Rule: of two past actions, the earlier one takes had + V3 (past perfect) and the later one takes the simple past.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "have shared" (present perfect) cannot be used with a finished past time marker such as "in 1986".

• Option 3 "sharing" is a bare participle and leaves the relative clause without a finite verb.

• Option 4 "shared" (simple past) is not wrong in casual usage but fails to show that the sharing was prior to "smelled", which is the sense the sentence needs.

NOTE

• Past perfect = had + past participle (V3): had shared, had gone, had written. It is the "past of the past".

• Present perfect (have/has + V3) is never used with a definite past time expression (yesterday, in 1986, last year).

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Much of the art he / discusses is funny, playing / and mischievous.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. discusses is funny, playing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The three words joined by "and" must be parallel — they must all be adjectives describing the art: "funny", "___" and "mischievous". "playing" is a participle/gerund, not an adjective, so it breaks the parallelism. The correct adjective is "playful".

◦ Correct: Much of the art he discusses is funny, playful and mischievous.

• "Playful" means light-hearted, full of fun, not serious. (चंचल / विनोदपूर्ण)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Segment 4 "Much of the art he" is correct — "much of" is rightly used with the uncountable noun "art", and it takes the singular verb "is".

• Segment 1 "and mischievous." is correct — "mischievous" (शरारती) is a proper adjective and is correctly spelt (note: NOT "mischievious").

• Option 2 "No error" is wrong because the parallelism error is present.

NOTE

• Rule of parallelism: items joined by and/or/but must belong to the same grammatical class — adjective + adjective + adjective, or noun + noun + noun, or V-ing + V-ing + V-ing.

• Use "much of" with uncountable nouns (much of the water) and "many of" with countable plurals (many of the students).

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Valiance
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Gallantry.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Valiance" (from "valiant") means bravery, courage and boldness, especially in battle. (वीरता / शौर्य)

• Its closest synonym is "Gallantry", which also means courageous behaviour, heroic bravery. (शौर्य)

◦ Example: The soldier was decorated for his valiance/gallantry on the battlefield.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Cravenness" means cowardice; a contemptible lack of courage — an antonym. (कायरता)

• Option 3 "Dastardliness" means wicked cowardice; despicable behaviour — also an antonym. (नीचता / कायरता)

• Option 4 "Patience" means the ability to endure delay calmly — unrelated to courage. (धैर्य)

NOTE

• Synonyms of valiance/valour: gallantry, bravery, heroism, fortitude, intrepidity, mettle.

• Antonyms: cowardice, timidity, cravenness, faint-heartedness.

• India's gallantry awards: Param Vir Chakra, Maha Vir Chakra, Vir Chakra (wartime) and Ashoka Chakra, Kirti Chakra, Shaurya Chakra (peacetime).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Buy a lemon
option_2: The ability to know what's happening
option_4: To buy something that is worthless
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To buy something that is worthless.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "buy a lemon" means to purchase something (typically a vehicle or gadget) that turns out to be defective, useless or worthless. (बेकार/खराब चीज़ ख़रीद लेना)

◦ Example: That second-hand car broke down in a week — I really bought a lemon.

• In informal English a "lemon" by itself means a useless or faulty product.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Wear fashionable clothing" corresponds to idioms like "dressed to kill" or "dressed to the nines".

• Option 2 "The ability to know what's happening" is closer to "have one's finger on the pulse" or "be in the know".

• Option 3 "To not complain" matches "grin and bear it" or "take it on the chin".

NOTE

• Other "money/buying" idioms: "pay through the nose" (pay far too much), "a rip-off" (something overpriced), "cost an arm and a leg" (be very expensive), "a white elephant" (a costly but useless possession).

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Some plants secrete oils during dry periods, and when it rains, these oils are released on the air.
option_1: these oils are released on the air.
option_2: dry periods, and when it rains,
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. these oils are released on the air.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct preposition with "air" here is "into" (movement/release into a medium), not "on". So the segment should read "these oils are released into the air".

◦ Correct: ... when it rains, these oils are released into the air.

• "Release into the air/atmosphere/water" is the standard collocation for something being discharged into a surrounding medium.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Segment 3 "Some plants secrete oils during" is correct — "secrete" (to produce and discharge a substance) is rightly used with "during + a period".

• Segment 2 "dry periods, and when it rains," is correct — the impersonal "it rains" is standard.

• Option 4 "No error" is wrong because of the preposition mistake.

NOTE

• Preposition notes: in the air (present/floating in the air), on air (being broadcast on radio/TV), into the air (movement outward/upward). Gases and pollutants are always released into the air.

• Do not confuse "secrete" (to discharge, e.g., glands secrete hormones) with "secret" (hidden).

question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given.

Now, (how much autograph) would you like? I can do joined-up writing now, you know!'
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. how many autographs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Autograph" is a countable noun, so the correct question word is "how many", not "how much", and the noun must be plural — "how many autographs".

◦ Correct: Now, how many autographs would you like? I can do joined-up writing now, you know!

• Rule: how many + countable plural noun (how many books, how many autographs); how much + uncountable noun (how much water, how much money).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "No correction required" is wrong because "how much autograph" is doubly faulty (wrong quantifier + singular noun).

• Option 1 "how most autographs" is not an English structure — "most" cannot follow "how" in a question.

• Option 3 "how much many autographs" wrongly stacks two quantifiers together.

NOTE

• Quantifiers with countables: many, few, a few, several, a number of.

• Quantifiers with uncountables: much, little, a little, a great deal of, an amount of.

• Common with both: some, any, a lot of, plenty of, all, most.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

The water leaked in with a hole in the roof.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. through a hole.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When something passes from one side of an opening to the other, the correct preposition is "through". Water enters "through a hole", not "with a hole".

◦ Correct: The water leaked in through a hole in the roof.

• "Through" expresses movement from one end/side to the other of an opening, passage or medium. (के आर-पार / के ज़रिए)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No improvement" is wrong — "with a hole" wrongly suggests instrument/accompaniment.

• Option 2 "by a holed" is meaningless; "holed" is not a noun.

• Option 3 "through a holes" mixes the singular article "a" with the plural noun "holes" — an article–number mismatch.

NOTE

• Preposition contrasts: through (through the tunnel, through the window), across (across the road — from one side to the other on a surface), over (over the wall), into (into the room), along (along the river).

• "With" denotes an instrument or accompaniment (cut it with a knife), which is not the sense required here.

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

One who makes an active effort to promote human welfare
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Philanthropist.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Philanthropist" is a person who actively works for and donates to the welfare of humanity, usually by giving money to good causes. (परोपकारी / लोकहितैषी)

◦ Example: The philanthropist donated crores of rupees for schools and hospitals.

• Word roots: philos = loving + anthropos = mankind → "lover of mankind".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Misogynist" is a person who hates or is strongly prejudiced against women. (स्त्री-द्वेषी)

• Option 3 "Sexist" is a person who discriminates on the basis of sex/gender.

• Option 4 "Feminist" is a person who supports equal rights for women. (नारीवादी)

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: Misanthrope (one who hates mankind), Philanthropy (love of mankind/charity), Altruist (one who selflessly works for others), Misogamist (one who hates marriage), Philanderer (one who flirts).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Everyone who studies forests knows trees have been dying in large and _______ numbers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. massive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is joined by "and" to "large", so it must carry a similar, reinforcing sense of great quantity. "Massive" means very large in size, amount or number; huge. (विशाल / भारी)

◦ Correct: ... trees have been dying in large and massive numbers.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "peculiar" means strange/odd — it does not describe quantity.

• Option 2 "minority" is a noun meaning the smaller part of a group; it cannot function as an adjective before "numbers" here.

• Option 4 "scanty" means very small in amount, barely sufficient — the exact opposite of "large", so it contradicts the sentence. (अल्प / कम)

NOTE

• Synonyms of massive: huge, enormous, colossal, immense, vast, gigantic.

• Antonyms: tiny, minute, scanty, meagre, negligible.

• Words joined by "and" should agree in sense; a word of contrasting meaning would need "but" instead.

question:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Proceed
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Withdraw.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Proceed" means to go forward, advance or continue with an action. (आगे बढ़ना)

• Its antonym is "Withdraw", which means to move back, retreat or pull out. (पीछे हटना / वापस लेना)

◦ Example: The army was ordered to proceed towards the border, but bad weather forced it to withdraw.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Wide" (broad) and Option 3 "Local" (of a particular area) are unrelated to forward/backward movement.

• Option 4 "Accidental" (happening by chance) is also unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of proceed: advance, continue, carry on, progress, move on.

• Antonyms of proceed: withdraw, retreat, recede, stop, halt, discontinue.

• Note the spelling family: proceed, exceed, succeed take "-ceed"; most others take "-cede" (recede, precede, concede).

question: Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Discribe.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Discribe" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Describe", meaning to give an account of something in words; to tell what someone or something is like. (वर्णन करना)

◦ Correct: Please describe the scene in your own words.

• Spelling key: DE + SCRIBE (from Latin scribere = to write).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Melting" (turning from solid to liquid), "Advance" (to move forward / progress) and "Start" (to begin) are all spelt correctly.

NOTE

• The "-scribe/-script" family (all from scribere, to write): describe, prescribe, subscribe, inscribe, transcribe, ascribe, manuscript, script.

• Related forms of describe: description (noun), descriptive (adjective) — note that the noun switches to "-scription".

question:
Select the appropriate synonym for the underlined word.

He wasn't entirely convinced.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. accepting.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Convinced" means firmly persuaded of the truth of something; certain and believing. (आश्वस्त / विश्वस्त)

• The closest synonym among the options is "accepting", i.e., willing to believe or agree with something.

◦ Example: After hearing the evidence he was convinced/accepting of her innocence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "doubting" (uncertain, sceptical) is an antonym of convinced.

• Option 4 "trustless" (not trusting / not to be trusted) is also opposite in sense.

• Option 2 "submerged" (under water; covered over) is completely unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of convinced: certain, persuaded, satisfied, sure, positive, assured.

• Antonyms: doubtful, sceptical, unconvinced, dubious, hesitant.

• Verb forms: convince (to persuade), conviction (a firm belief — also a court verdict of guilt).

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

My parents used to encouraged me to devote more time to study.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. encourage me to devote.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Used to" is always followed by the base form (V1) of the verb, never by the past form. So "used to encouraged" is wrong; it must be "used to encourage".

◦ Correct: My parents used to encourage me to devote more time to study.

• The pattern "encourage + object + to + V1" ("encourage me to devote") is also correct and must be retained.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "No improvement" is wrong because "used to encouraged" is ungrammatical.

• Option 1 "encouraging me devoting" leaves the sentence without a proper finite structure and drops the necessary "to".

• Option 3 "encourages me to devote" wrongly puts a present-tense third-person "-s" form after "used to".

NOTE

• "Used to + V1" expresses a past habit or a past state that is no longer true: He used to smoke. She used to live here.

• Do not confuse it with "be/get used to + V-ing/noun" (= be accustomed to): He is used to working at night.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

When Jane died (1) ______ 1850, she was called “one of the most distinguished novelists (2) ______ England has produced” and “the first who (3) ______ that beautiful kind of fiction, the historical romance.” The Porter sisters’ careers ended (4) ______ as the Brontë sisters were getting started in the early Victorian (5) ______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. in.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• With a year, the preposition of time is always "in" — in 1850, in 2023, in the nineteenth century.

◦ Correct: When Jane died in 1850, she was called ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "on" is used with days and dates — on Monday, on 5 May 1850.

• Option 3 "at" is used with exact points of time — at 6 o'clock, at noon, at midnight.

• Option 4 "into" shows movement inside something and is not a preposition of time.

NOTE

• Prepositions of time — the "AT–ON–IN" ladder (smallest to largest): AT a time (at 5 p.m.), ON a day/date (on Sunday), IN a month/year/season/century (in June, in 1850, in summer).

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

When Jane died (1) ______ 1850, she was called “one of the most distinguished novelists (2) ______ England has produced” and “the first who (3) ______ that beautiful kind of fiction, the historical romance.” The Porter sisters’ careers ended (4) ______ as the Brontë sisters were getting started in the early Victorian (5) ______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. which.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The relative pronoun refers back to "novelists" and is the object of the verb "has produced" ("England has produced [the novelists]"). For the object of a clause, "which" (or "that"/"whom") is used, and here "which" is the option given.

◦ Correct: ... one of the most distinguished novelists which England has produced ...

• Note that the relative pronoun here is not the subject — "England" is the subject — so a subject pronoun is not needed.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "who" would have to be the subject of "has produced", which is impossible because "England" already occupies that slot.

• Option 2 "what" is never used as a relative pronoun after a stated antecedent (novelists).

• Option 3 "whose" is possessive and would require a noun after it (whose novels), which is absent.

NOTE

• Relative pronouns: who (subject, persons), whom (object, persons), which (things/animals; also used after superlatives in older/formal style), whose (possessive), that (persons or things, especially after superlatives).

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

When Jane died (1) ______ 1850, she was called “one of the most distinguished novelists (2) ______ England has produced” and “the first who (3) ______ that beautiful kind of fiction, the historical romance.” The Porter sisters’ careers ended (4) ______ as the Brontë sisters were getting started in the early Victorian (5) ______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. introduced.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage praises Jane as "the first who ______ that beautiful kind of fiction, the historical romance". Being the first person associated with a genre means she brought it in / started it — so "introduced" fits perfectly. (प्रस्तुत करना / आरंभ करना)

◦ Correct: ... the first who introduced that beautiful kind of fiction, the historical romance.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "dismissed" (rejected/sent away) contradicts the praise being given.

• Option 3 "casted" is not a standard form — the past tense of "cast" is "cast"; moreover "cast" does not collocate with a kind of fiction.

• Option 4 "energized" (gave energy to) does not fit the idea of originating a literary genre.

NOTE

• Verbs with the same form in all three parts (V1 = V2 = V3): cast, cost, cut, hit, hurt, let, put, set, shut, spread, burst, read (pronunciation changes for "read").

• Collocations with "introduce": introduce a reform / a bill / a new genre / a product / a person.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

When Jane died (1) ______ 1850, she was called “one of the most distinguished novelists (2) ______ England has produced” and “the first who (3) ______ that beautiful kind of fiction, the historical romance.” The Porter sisters’ careers ended (4) ______ as the Brontë sisters were getting started in the early Victorian (5) ______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. just.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence contrasts two events happening at almost the same moment — one career ending exactly when another was beginning. The adverb "just" before "as" means "at the very moment that", which conveys this precisely.

◦ Correct: The Porter sisters' careers ended just as the Brontë sisters were getting started ...

• "Just as" = at exactly the same time as. (ठीक उसी समय जब)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "lest" means "for fear that / in case" and is followed by "should" — it does not fit a time contrast.

• Option 3 "that" would create "ended that as", which is ungrammatical.

• Option 4 "must" is a modal verb and cannot stand before "as" in this way.

NOTE

• Time connectors: just as (at that very moment), as soon as (immediately after), while (during the same period), by the time (before/at the moment when), no sooner ... than (immediately after).

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

When Jane died (1) ______ 1850, she was called “one of the most distinguished novelists (2) ______ England has produced” and “the first who (3) ______ that beautiful kind of fiction, the historical romance.” The Porter sisters’ careers ended (4) ______ as the Brontë sisters were getting started in the early Victorian (5) ______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. period.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Victorian period" is the standard historical expression for the era of Queen Victoria's reign (1837–1901). A "period" is a stretch of time in history marked by particular characteristics. (काल / युग)

◦ Correct: ... as the Brontë sisters were getting started in the early Victorian period.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "terms" is plural and refers to school/court terms or conditions of an agreement — it does not name a historical era.

• Option 3 "session" means a meeting or sitting (a court session, a parliamentary session), not a historical age.

• Option 4 "spell" means a short stretch of time or weather (a spell of rain, a dry spell) and is too brief and informal for a historical era.

NOTE

• Literary/historical eras of English: Elizabethan (1558–1603), Jacobean, Restoration, Romantic (c. 1798–1837), Victorian (1837–1901), Modern (20th century).

• The Brontë sisters — Charlotte (Jane Eyre), Emily (Wuthering Heights) and Anne — wrote in the early Victorian period.

question: The Election Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2021 belongs to __________ Ministry of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Law and Justice.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Election Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2021 was introduced in the Lok Sabha by the Ministry of Law and Justice. (विधि एवं न्याय मंत्रालय)

• The Bill amended the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and 1951, mainly to allow the linking of the electoral roll data with the Aadhaar ecosystem on a voluntary basis, to curb duplicate and bogus entries.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other key provisions: it made the qualifying dates for enrolment four in a year (1 January, 1 April, 1 July, 1 October) instead of only 1 January, and it made the service-voter provisions gender-neutral (replacing "wife" with "spouse").

• The Bill was passed by Parliament in December 2021.

• The Ministry of Law and Justice is the oldest limb of the Government of India, comprising the Legislative Department, Department of Legal Affairs and Department of Justice.

NOTE

• Elections in India are conducted by the Election Commission of India (Article 324), a constitutional body set up on 25 January 1950 — observed as National Voters' Day.

question: Rukmini Devi Arundale was a famous exponent of which form of dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatnatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rukmini Devi Arundale (1904–1986) was the celebrated exponent and reviver of Bharatanatyam, the classical dance of Tamil Nadu. (भरतनाट्यम)

• She removed the social stigma attached to the dance, took it from the temple to the proscenium stage and gave it respectability in modern India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• In 1936 she founded "Kalakshetra" near Chennai, an institution devoted to the teaching of classical dance and music; it is now an Institute of National Importance.

• She was awarded the Padma Bhushan (1956) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship, and was also a member of the Rajya Sabha and a noted animal-welfare activist (she piloted the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960).

NOTE

• Bharatanatyam is based on the Natya Shastra of Bharata Muni; its main elements are Nritta (pure dance), Nritya (expressive dance) and Natya (drama).

• The eight classical dances: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (UP), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

question: Which river is also known as Dakshin Ganga?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Godavari.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Godavari is known as the "Dakshin Ganga" (the Ganga of the South) because it is the largest river of peninsular India and holds the same religious importance in the south that the Ganga holds in the north. (दक्षिण गंगा — गोदावरी)

• It rises at Trimbakeshwar near Nashik (Maharashtra) in the Western Ghats and flows east for about 1,465 km into the Bay of Bengal.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• It is the second longest river in India after the Ganga, and the longest in peninsular India.

• States in its basin: Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Karnataka and Puducherry (Yanam).

• Main tributaries: Pravara, Purna, Manjira, Indravati, Pranhita, Sabari.

• The Kumbh Mela at Nashik is held on its banks.

NOTE

• Other peninsular rivers: Krishna (rises at Mahabaleshwar), Kaveri ("Dakshin Bharat ki Ganga", rises at Talakaveri, Karnataka), Tungabhadra (a tributary of the Krishna), Mahanadi (Chhattisgarh/Odisha).

question: 'A Life of the Genius: The Man Who Knew Infinity' is a biography of Indian mathematician ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Srinivasa Ramanujan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Man Who Knew Infinity: A Life of the Genius Ramanujan" is the celebrated biography of the Indian mathematical genius Srinivasa Ramanujan, written by Robert Kanigel (1991). (श्रीनिवास रामानुजन)

• A film of the same name, starring Dev Patel as Ramanujan, was released in 2015.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Srinivasa Ramanujan (1887–1920) was born at Erode, Tamil Nadu. With almost no formal training in pure mathematics he made extraordinary contributions to number theory, infinite series, continued fractions and mathematical analysis.

• He was invited to Cambridge by G. H. Hardy and became one of the youngest Fellows of the Royal Society (1918).

• 1729 is called the Hardy–Ramanujan number (the smallest number expressible as the sum of two cubes in two different ways: 1³+12³ = 9³+10³).

NOTE

• His birthday, 22 December, is celebrated as National Mathematics Day in India.

• Other mathematicians in the options: Acharya Pingala (ancient scholar of prosody, linked with binary numbers and the "Meru Prastara"/Pascal's triangle), Aryabhata (author of Aryabhatiya, value of π), Neena Gupta (won the Ramanujan Prize 2021 for solving the Zariski cancellation problem).

question: Which harvest festival is famously celebrated in Assam?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhogali Bihu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bhogali Bihu" (also called Magh Bihu) is the harvest festival of Assam, celebrated in the month of Magh (mid-January) to mark the end of the harvesting season. (भोगाली बिहू — असम)

• "Bhog" means eating and enjoyment, so the festival is marked by feasting, community meals, the building of temporary huts called "Meji" and "Bhelaghar", bonfires, and traditional games like buffalo fights and egg fights.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Assam celebrates three Bihus: Rongali/Bohag Bihu (April — the Assamese New Year and spring festival), Bhogali/Magh Bihu (January — harvest) and Kongali/Kati Bihu (October — a sombre, austere one).

• Other harvest festivals: Lohri (Punjab), Makar Sankranti (nationwide/Gujarat–Maharashtra), Pongal (Tamil Nadu), Onam (Kerala), Baisakhi (Punjab), Nuakhai (Odisha).

NOTE

• Since all these fall around mid-January, examiners test the state–festival pairing: the question asks specifically about Assam, so Bhogali Bihu is the answer.

question: Which among the following socio religious community was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brahmo Samaj.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the "Brahmo Samaj" in 1828 at Calcutta (it began as the Atmiya Sabha, 1815, and then the Brahmo Sabha, 1828). (ब्रह्म समाज — 1828)

• The Brahmo Samaj preached monotheism, opposed idol worship, casteism, polytheism and meaningless rituals, and drew on the Upanishads as well as on rational thought.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy is called the "Father of the Indian Renaissance" and the "Maker of Modern India". His greatest achievement was the abolition of Sati in 1829 with the help of Governor-General Lord William Bentinck.

• He started the newspapers Sambad Kaumudi (Bengali) and Mirat-ul-Akhbar (Persian), and the title "Raja" was conferred on him by the Mughal emperor Akbar II.

NOTE

• Other reform bodies: Prarthana Samaj (1867, Bombay — Atmaram Pandurang), Arya Samaj (1875, Bombay — Swami Dayanand Saraswati, "Back to the Vedas"), Ramakrishna Mission (1897 — Swami Vivekananda), Satyashodhak Samaj (1873 — Jyotiba Phule).

question: When the British rule ended in India in the year 1947 the literacy rate was just ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 12 percent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• At the time of Independence in 1947, India's literacy rate was only about 12 per cent — a legacy of the neglect of mass education under colonial rule. (1947 में साक्षरता दर लगभग 12 प्रतिशत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Literacy has risen steadily since then: 18.33% (1951) → 28.3% (1961) → 52.21% (1991) → 64.83% (2001) → 74.04% (Census 2011).

• As per Census 2011, Kerala had the highest literacy rate (94%) and Bihar the lowest (61.8%); male literacy was 82.14% and female literacy 65.46%.

• A person aged 7 years and above who can read and write with understanding in any language is counted as literate.

NOTE

• Key education initiatives: Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (2001), the Right to Education Act, 2009 (Article 21A — free and compulsory education for ages 6–14), Samagra Shiksha, and the National Education Policy, 2020.

question: Cells were first observed in cork by ______ in 1665.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Robert Hooke.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 1665, the English scientist Robert Hooke examined a thin slice of cork under his self-designed microscope and saw tiny box-like compartments, which he named "cells" (from the Latin cellula, meaning "a little room"). (रॉबर्ट हुक — 1665, कोशिका)

• He published this discovery in his famous book "Micrographia". What he actually saw were the dead cell walls of cork tissue.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Anton van Leeuwenhoek (1674) was the first to observe living cells — bacteria and protozoa ("animalcules") — and is called the "Father of Microbiology".

• Robert Brown (1831) discovered the nucleus; Purkinje (1839) coined the term "protoplasm".

• The Cell Theory was proposed by Schleiden (1838) and Schwann (1839), and completed by Rudolf Virchow (1855) with "Omnis cellula-e cellula" (all cells arise from pre-existing cells).

NOTE

• Theophrastus is called the "Father of Botany"; Edward Jenner developed the smallpox vaccine (1796) and is called the "Father of Immunology".

question: Ustad Shafaat Ahmed Khan was best known for which of the following instrument?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tabla.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Shafaat Ahmed Khan (1958–2015) was a celebrated Indian tabla maestro of the Delhi Gharana. (तबला वादक)

• He accompanied many leading vocalists and instrumentalists and was awarded the Padma Shri (2006) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The tabla is a pair of hand drums — the smaller right-hand drum is the "dayan/tabla" (wooden) and the larger left-hand one is the "bayan/dagga" (metal). It is the principal percussion instrument of Hindustani classical music.

• Its invention is traditionally attributed to Amir Khusrau.

• Famous tabla players: Ustad Zakir Hussain, Ustad Alla Rakha, Pandit Kishan Maharaj, Pandit Samta Prasad, Pandit Anindo Chatterjee.

NOTE

• Classification of instruments: Avanaddha Vadya (percussion — tabla, mridangam, pakhawaj), Tata Vadya (string — sitar, sarod, veena), Sushira Vadya (wind — flute, shehnai), Ghana Vadya (solid/struck — manjira, jaltarang).

question: Which is the oldest tennis tournament in the world?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Wimbledon.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Wimbledon", first held in 1877 at the All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club, London, is the oldest tennis tournament in the world. (विंबलडन — 1877)

• It is the only Grand Slam still played on grass courts, and it has a strict all-white dress code for players.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The four Grand Slam tournaments and their surfaces/years of origin:

◦ Australian Open (1905) — hard court, January, Melbourne.

◦ French Open / Roland Garros (1891) — clay court, May–June, Paris.

◦ Wimbledon (1877) — grass court, June–July, London.

◦ US Open (1881) — hard court, August–September, New York.

NOTE

• Indian Grand Slam winners (doubles/mixed doubles) include Leander Paes, Mahesh Bhupathi, Rohan Bopanna, Sania Mirza and Divij Sharan. Ramanathan Krishnan and Vijay Amritraj were India's early singles stars.

question: Gorakhpur is the headquarter of _______ Railway of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is North-Eastern.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gorakhpur (Uttar Pradesh) is the headquarters of the North Eastern Railway (NER) zone of Indian Railways. (उत्तर पूर्व रेलवे — गोरखपुर)

• Gorakhpur Junction is also famous for having one of the world's longest railway platforms (about 1,355 m).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Some important zonal headquarters:

◦ Northern Railway – New Delhi; Eastern Railway – Kolkata; Western Railway – Mumbai (Churchgate).

◦ Central Railway – Mumbai (CSMT); Southern Railway – Chennai; South Central Railway – Secunderabad.

◦ North Eastern Railway – Gorakhpur; Northeast Frontier Railway – Maligaon (Guwahati); North Central Railway – Prayagraj.

• Indian Railways currently has 18 zones (including the Kolkata Metro Railway).

NOTE

• Indian Railways is the fourth largest rail network in the world. The first passenger train in India ran on 16 April 1853 from Bori Bunder (Mumbai) to Thane, a distance of about 34 km.

question: The reaction between an acid and a base is known as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neutralisation reaction.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The reaction between an acid and a base that produces salt and water is called a "neutralisation reaction". (उदासीनीकरण अभिक्रिया)

◦ General form: Acid + Base → Salt + Water

◦ Example: HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O

• The essential change is that H⁺ ions from the acid combine with OH⁻ ions from the base to form water, so the acidic and basic properties are cancelled out.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Everyday examples: taking an antacid (milk of magnesia) for acidity in the stomach, applying baking soda on an ant/bee sting, and adding lime to acidic soil.

• Oxidation is loss of electrons/addition of oxygen; condensation joins two molecules with the loss of a small molecule such as water; "sub-alteration" is not a chemical term.

NOTE

• pH scale (0–14): below 7 = acidic, 7 = neutral, above 7 = basic. A neutralisation reaction moves the solution towards pH 7.

• Acids turn blue litmus red; bases turn red litmus blue.

question: Who was the court poet of Harshavardhana?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Banabhatta.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Banabhatta was the court poet (Asthana Kavi) of Emperor Harshavardhana (r. 606–647 CE) of the Pushyabhuti/Vardhana dynasty of Thanesar–Kannauj. (बाणभट्ट — हर्षवर्धन का दरबारी कवि)

• His two famous Sanskrit works are:

◦ "Harshacharita" — a biography of Harsha, the first historical biography in Sanskrit.

◦ "Kadambari" — regarded as one of the earliest novels in world literature.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Harshavardhana himself was a scholar and wrote three Sanskrit plays — "Ratnavali", "Nagananda" and "Priyadarshika".

• The Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang) visited India during Harsha's reign and described it in his account "Si-Yu-Ki".

• Harsha was defeated by the Chalukya king Pulakesin II on the banks of the Narmada.

NOTE

• Famous court poets: Kalidasa (Chandragupta II Vikramaditya), Banabhatta (Harsha), Kalhana (author of Rajatarangini), Amir Khusrau (Delhi Sultans), Abul Fazl (Akbar).

question: Which union territory has a high court of its own?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Delhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Delhi (the National Capital Territory of Delhi) is the only Union Territory that has a High Court of its own — the Delhi High Court, established in 1966. (दिल्ली उच्च न्यायालय — 1966)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The other UTs fall under the jurisdiction of the High Courts of neighbouring states:

◦ Chandigarh → Punjab and Haryana High Court.

◦ Andaman and Nicobar Islands → Calcutta High Court.

◦ Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu → Bombay High Court.

◦ Puducherry → Madras High Court; Lakshadweep → Kerala High Court.

◦ Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh → the common High Court of J&K and Ladakh.

• Article 214 provides for a High Court for each state; Article 231 allows a common High Court for two or more states/UTs.

NOTE

• India's oldest High Courts (all established in 1862): Calcutta, Bombay and Madras. Delhi is unique among UTs because of its special status under Article 239AA.

question: Unemployment caused by the recession of 2008-2010 is an example of which of the following types of unemployment?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cyclical.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Cyclical unemployment is unemployment caused by a downturn in the business cycle — during a recession or depression, aggregate demand falls, output shrinks and firms lay off workers. (चक्रीय बेरोज़गारी)

• The global recession of 2008–2010, triggered by the collapse of the US sub-prime housing market, is the classic example of cyclical unemployment.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Frictional unemployment — the short, temporary gap while a person moves between jobs or enters the labour force.

• Structural unemployment — arises when workers' skills do not match the jobs available, due to technological change or a shift in the economy's structure.

• Classical (real-wage) unemployment — occurs when wages are kept above the market-clearing level, so employers hire fewer workers.

• Disguised unemployment — more people are engaged in a job than actually needed (common in Indian agriculture); seasonal unemployment — work is available only in certain seasons.

NOTE

• Cyclical unemployment is remedied by expansionary fiscal and monetary policy (higher government spending, tax cuts, lower interest rates) that raises aggregate demand — a core idea of Keynesian economics.

question: Bahmani Monuments at Gulbarga, Karnataka represent __________ style of architecture.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Deccan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bahmani monuments at Gulbarga (Kalaburagi), Karnataka represent the "Deccan" style of Indo-Islamic architecture — a provincial style that blended Persian, Turkish and local Indian features. (दक्कन शैली)

• The Jama Masjid at Gulbarga is its most famous example: it is unusual in that its entire courtyard is covered by a roof of domes, a feature rare in Indian mosques.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Bahmani Sultanate was founded in 1347 by Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah (Hasan Gangu), with its capital first at Gulbarga and later at Bidar.

• The famous minister Mahmud Gawan built the Madrasa at Bidar, a splendid example of Persian-influenced architecture.

• The Bahmani kingdom later split into five Deccan Sultanates — Bijapur (Adil Shahi), Ahmadnagar (Nizam Shahi), Golconda (Qutb Shahi), Bidar (Barid Shahi) and Berar (Imad Shahi).

NOTE

• Indo-Islamic provincial styles: Delhi/Imperial, Bengal, Jaunpur, Gujarat, Malwa, Bijapur and Deccan.

• Nagara (North Indian), Dravida (South Indian) and Vesara (a hybrid) are the styles of temple architecture, not Islamic monuments.

question: Who was the founder of Prarthana Samaj?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Atmaram Pandurang.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Prarthana Samaj" was founded in 1867 at Bombay by Dr. Atmaram Pandurang, with the inspiration and guidance of Keshab Chandra Sen of the Brahmo Samaj. (प्रार्थना समाज — 1867, आत्माराम पांडुरंग)

• It worked for theistic worship, the abolition of caste, widow remarriage, women's education and the raising of the age of marriage.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Its most illustrious members were Mahadev Govind Ranade, R. G. Bhandarkar and N. G. Chandavarkar. Ranade also founded the Deccan Education Society and the Widow Remarriage Association.

• The Prarthana Samaj drew heavily on the Bhakti tradition of Maharashtra's saints (Tukaram, Namdev), which made it socially acceptable in western India.

NOTE

• Other socio-religious movements: Brahmo Samaj (1828 — Raja Ram Mohan Roy), Arya Samaj (1875 — Dayanand Saraswati), Ramakrishna Mission (1897 — Swami Vivekananda), Namdhari/Kuka movement (Ram Singh), Theosophical Society (1875 — Blavatsky and Olcott).

question: The forces which act in the interior of the earth are called as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is endogenic forces.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The forces that operate inside/within the earth are called "endogenic (internal) forces". (अंतर्जात बल)

• They derive their energy mainly from the earth's internal heat (radioactivity, primordial heat, rotational and tidal friction) and are responsible for building up the surface — creating mountains, plateaus, faults, folds, earthquakes and volcanoes.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Endogenic forces are of two kinds:

◦ Diastrophic (slow) forces — epeirogenic (vertical, continent-building) and orogenic (horizontal, mountain-building through folding and faulting).

◦ Sudden forces — earthquakes and volcanic eruptions.

• "Exogenic (external) forces" act on the surface — weathering, erosion, transportation and deposition by rivers, glaciers, wind and waves. They level down the surface.

NOTE

• Endogenic forces are constructive (they build relief), while exogenic forces are destructive/gradational (they wear it down). The two together shape the earth's relief — a process called gradation.

question: How many field players are in a hockey team?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 11.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A field hockey team consists of 11 players on the field at a time. (हॉकी — 11 खिलाड़ी)

• The eleven normally comprise a goalkeeper, defenders, midfielders and forwards, and a team is additionally allowed a pool of substitutes (usually 5, making a squad of 16), with rolling substitutions permitted.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Hockey is the national game association most identified with India; India won 8 Olympic gold medals in hockey (1928, 1932, 1936, 1948, 1952, 1956, 1964, 1980) and a bronze at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024.

• Major Dhyan Chand, the "Wizard of Hockey", was born on 29 August, celebrated as National Sports Day. India's highest sporting honour is the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award.

• A hockey match is played in four quarters of 15 minutes each; the governing body is the International Hockey Federation (FIH), and India's is Hockey India.

NOTE

• Number of players in other sports: Cricket 11, Football 11, Hockey 11, Volleyball 6, Basketball 5, Kabaddi 7, Kho-Kho 9 (12 in a squad), Water Polo 7, Baseball 9, Polo 4.

question: The intervention of the government whether to expand demand or reduce it constitutes the ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is stabilisation function.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The government's decision to expand or contract aggregate demand in order to control inflation, unemployment and fluctuations in the business cycle is known as the "stabilisation function" of the budget. (स्थिरीकरण कार्य)

• When there is a recession, the government raises spending / cuts taxes to expand demand; when there is inflation, it cuts spending / raises taxes to reduce demand.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The three classic functions of the government budget (Musgrave's classification):

◦ Allocation function — providing public goods (defence, roads, street lighting) that the market fails to supply.

◦ Redistribution function — reducing inequality through progressive taxation and transfer payments/subsidies.

◦ Stabilisation function — maintaining economic stability, full employment and price stability.

NOTE

• The Union Budget is presented under Article 112 (Annual Financial Statement). Since 2017 it is presented on 1 February, and the Railway Budget has been merged with it.

• Fiscal policy = government's tax and spending policy; monetary policy = the RBI's control of money supply and interest rates.

question: During the Sultanate of Delhi, the term "Ulema" was associated with ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Learned theologians and Jurists.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• During the Delhi Sultanate, the "Ulema" (singular alim) were the learned men of Islamic theology and law (jurists). (उलेमा — धर्मशास्त्री एवं विधिवेत्ता)

• They interpreted the Shariat, advised the Sultan on religious and legal matters, and held key offices such as Qazi (judge), Mufti (jurisconsult), Sadr and Muhtasib. They formed an extremely influential class in the state.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Sultans such as Balban and Firoz Shah Tughlaq were guided by the Ulema, whereas Alauddin Khalji deliberately kept them out of state affairs, declaring that he framed rules for the good of the state, not on their advice.

• Other administrative terms of the period:

◦ Ariz-i-Mamalik — head of the military department (the commander-in-chief was the Sultan himself).

◦ Barid — intelligence/postal officer; Diwan-i-Insha — the department of royal correspondence.

◦ Muqaddam / Chaudhari / Khut — village and local revenue officials.

NOTE

• The Delhi Sultanate (1206–1526) saw five dynasties: Slave/Mamluk, Khalji, Tughlaq, Sayyid and Lodi. It ended with Ibrahim Lodi's defeat at the First Battle of Panipat (1526) by Babur.

question: Which plant tissue is responsible for the transportation of water and minerals from the soil to the stems and leaves?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Xylem.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Xylem" is the complex, conducting (vascular) tissue that carries water and dissolved minerals from the roots upward to the stem and leaves. (जाइलम — जल एवं खनिजों का संवहन)

• Its four components are tracheids, vessels (trachea), xylem parenchyma and xylem fibres. The conduction is unidirectional (upward) and is driven by root pressure and transpiration pull.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Phloem" is the other vascular tissue; it transports prepared food (sucrose) from the leaves to all other parts — a bidirectional process called translocation. It consists of sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma and phloem fibres.

• Parenchyma (simple, thin-walled, storage and photosynthesis), Collenchyma (living, thickened at corners, gives flexibility) and Sclerenchyma (dead, lignified, gives strength) are the simple permanent tissues.

NOTE

• Meristematic tissue (apical, intercalary, lateral) is responsible for growth; permanent tissue is simple or complex.

• The transpiration pull theory of water ascent was given by Dixon and Joly (cohesion–tension theory).

question: Who won the prestigious Abhinandan Saroja National Award 2021 by the National Institute of Indian Classical Dance?
solution_text:

IMPORTANT POINTS

question: Out of the following, which one is a fundamental right in the constitution of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Right to Freedom.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Right to Freedom" (Articles 19–22) is one of the six Fundamental Rights guaranteed by Part III of the Constitution of India. (स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार — अनुच्छेद 19–22)

◦ Article 19 guarantees six freedoms: speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession/occupation/trade.

◦ Article 20 — protection in respect of conviction for offences; Article 21 — protection of life and personal liberty; Article 21A — right to education; Article 22 — protection against arbitrary arrest and detention.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The six Fundamental Rights are:

◦ Right to Equality (Articles 14–18)

◦ Right to Freedom (Articles 19–22)

◦ Right against Exploitation (Articles 23–24)

◦ Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25–28)

◦ Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles 29–30)

◦ Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32) — called the "heart and soul of the Constitution" by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar.

• The Right to Property was removed from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment, 1978, and is now a legal right under Article 300A.

NOTE

• The Right to Vote is a constitutional/statutory right under Article 326, and the Right to Work is a Directive Principle under Article 41 — neither is a Fundamental Right.

• Fundamental Rights are borrowed from the Constitution of the USA (Bill of Rights).

question: Which state government launched the "Panchamrut Yojana"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Panchamrut Yojana" was launched by the Government of Uttar Pradesh. (पंचामृत योजना — उत्तर प्रदेश)

• It is a scheme of the Sugarcane Department that promotes five integrated farming techniques together for sugarcane cultivation, so as to raise productivity and farmers' income while saving water.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The five components ("Panchamrut" = a mixture of five elements) are:

◦ Trench method of sowing sugarcane,

◦ Co-cropping/inter-cropping with pulses, vegetables or mustard,

◦ Drip irrigation,

◦ Mulching with sugarcane leaves (instead of burning them), and

◦ Ratoon management (careful care of the re-grown crop).

• Uttar Pradesh is India's largest producer of sugarcane and sugar.

NOTE

• Other Uttar Pradesh schemes often asked about: Mission Shakti, Kanya Sumangala Yojana, One District One Product (ODOP) and Matri Bhoomi Yojana.
